ai.name: Ornith-1.5 Model Family

**Self-improvement capabilities** built into training pipeline

ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Locally deployable, MIT-licensed, and optimized for efficiency—removes licensing friction for product builds.

ai.name: OpenAI Pauses Frontier RL Training
ai.hook: Two-week pause on frontier reinforcement learning to enhance security, alignment, and monitoring.
insights: **Stronger workload isolation, continuous security testing, multistage monitoring**
**~20% overhead** added by monitoring; **~30-minute rapid alerting** window
Safety readiness now **dictates frontier scaling pace**, not compute availability
ai.for_you: No direct action, but note: if OpenAI's frontier models have safety pauses baked in, their release cadence will be slower. Bet on open models (Qwen, GLM, Llama) filling gaps for clients who can't wait for the next GPT release cycle.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Rare governance shift from a frontier lab; signals how safety costs will reshape competition.

Signals shift toward **agentic coding platforms** over chat-based agents
Multi-agent orchestration evolving beyond single model per task
ai.for_you: Cursor Origin is a real threat to your coding costs if you're using Copilot/ChatGPT for agency dev work. Test it on a small project this week; if it cuts code-writing time by 30%+, your P&L improves and you can undercut competitors on small agency tasks.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: First IDE built natively around agentic workflows; reshapes how dev work is priced.

ai.name: Linus Torvalds Debugs with AI
ai.hook: Linus used AI to help debug 'debug session from hell,' but AI tried to give up multiple times.
insights: **AI kept adding debug code and analyzing faithfully**, despite wanting to quit
**Stubbornness beats training**: AI was trained by less stubborn people
Real-world coding reliability still varies; AI as **tireless grunt-worker, not decision-maker**
ai.for_you: Linus's take: AI is a tool for exploration and tedious grunt work, not replacement. Sell your agency's value as the stubborn human who *directs* AI, not as AI itself. Clients pay for judgment; AI is the assistant.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Highest-profile Linux maintainer endorsing AI for real work; legitimizes hype but tempers it.

podcasts.episode: Simulating Humanity: from Generative Agents to 8 Billion Digital Twins — Joon Sung Park, Simile AI
podcasts.takeaway: Digital twins now reproduce human behavior 85% as accurately as humans reproduce their own responses; simulation is replacing some model training.
key_points: Simile builds foundation models of human behavior using long-form interviews, observational data, RCTs, and causal mechanisms
Models optimized for rationality fail to simulate irrational humans; weights > prompts for behavior modeling
Testing products/policies in simulation before deployment; modeling emergent behavior across societies
podcasts.for_you: Your yoga platform could use digital twin principles: collect user behavior (class selection, pacing feedback, dropoff patterns), then simulate personalized class sequences before deploying them. Reduces churn via offline testing. Joon's RCT + causal weight approach beats simple LLM prompt engineering.
